reason: This text fragment from Ezra describes the return from exile and rebuilding of the Temple. The passage portrays the Israelite community gathering in Jerusalem, with leaders (Zerubbabel, Joshua/Yeshua the high priest, priests, and Levites) actively organizing the reconstruction of the altar and Temple foundation. The people participate willingly in worship, offerings, and celebration. While the text mentions weeping among those who remembered the first Temple, this emotional response is directed toward the lost glory of the former Temple structure itself, not toward complaints against the leadership. The leaders are depicted respectfully and their authority is not questioned; the narrative shows cohesive community action guided by these leaders.
